text:
Maria Chen: Quick notification: I'm about to merge a TF refactor that hoists provider blocks into the root module and renames some outputs. Before I do, need a quick 👍 on provider pin approach and k8s secret mapping — a couple services read secret paths from module outputs, so want to avoid breaking consumers.

Devin Patel: What provider pin strategy are you planning? pin major.minor or exact? we had incidents when minors bumped unexpectedly.

Maria Chen: Planning to pin major.minor for most providers (e.g., version = "~> 4.8" for google). For AWS I'm pinning exact for now ("= 4.61.0") because 4.62 had a breaking change that impacted STS calls.

Alex Ramos: If you hoist providers, remember modules that expect aliased providers can break. Are you preserving alias mapping? e.g., provider.aws.us_east = aws { region = "us-east-1" alias = "us_east" }

Maria Chen: Yes preserving aliases. I'm adding a tiny compatibility shim in the root to re-declare the common aliases so downstream modules don't need changes immediately. Will push a small diff. Example: ```hcl
provider "aws" {
  alias  = "us_east"
  region = var.region_us_east
}
```

Tasha Li: On the k8s secret mapping: which output name changed? our ingress controller reads module.outputs.k8s_secret_path directly.

Maria Chen: Old output was `k8s_secret_path`; new module uses a nested map `secrets.k8s_mount_path`. To keep backcompat I added a top-level output that falls back to the old key: ```hcl
output "k8s_secret_path" {
  value = try(module.foo.secrets.k8s_mount_path, module.foo.k8s_secret_path)
}
```

Devin Patel: Nice. Two asks before merge: 1) add a short migration note in the PR describing consumer changes (map -> nested map) and the shim. 2) run a smoke plan on staging and attach the plan output.

Maria Chen: Yep will add the migration note. Running plan against staging now and will post results.

infra-bot: plan — staging — module-refactor — started by Maria Chen at 2024-06-15T12:45:02Z

Maria Chen: Plan completed. Small drift: 3 resources replaced (provider alias re-declare, output shim, module call updated). No state moves required. Snippet: ```~ module.foo.aws_iam_role.example (forces replacement)``` — nothing unexpected.

Alex Ramos: LGTM from my side. One minor: update module README to document `k8s_secret_path` shim so integrators aren't confused.

Tasha Li: :thumbsup: can you add a tiny test in infra-e2e that asserts the presence of `k8s_secret_path`? our deploy verifies that before creating k8s secrets.

Maria Chen: Will add the test. Final Q: should we regenerate the providers lockfile at the root or keep per-module lockfiles? I'm leaning to regenerate root lockfile so CI uses consistent provider versions across repos.

Devin Patel: Root lockfile regen makes sense for now. Run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` in a clean workspace and push the lockfile. Add a note in PR about the lockfile bump (it's noisy but intentional).

Maria Chen: Thanks — I'll regen the lockfile, add migration notes, update the README, add the infra-e2e check, and merge after CI + staging smoke pass. @Tasha @Alex please ping if you see anything post-merge.
